To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the process of the emergence of the national e-ID solution is the result of interaction of interests and resources between the financial and public sector.
financialization influences IT development in the public sector through the emergence of national ID solutions.

the financialization of e-ID solutions can be understood as a dialectic process that unfolds over time, driven by five mechanisms: (1) the convergence of interests between the public and the financial sector; (2) the convergence of resources; (3) the emergence of a governance solution as a result of the convergence; (4) the emergence of an interdependent relation between the public and financial sectors; and (5) a re-convergence between the sectors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay between public and private interests and resources and how they are mobilized to shape IT governance solutions.
how financialization affects the development of public IT and the role of the public sector in this process.
the interdependency of the financial sector and the public sector, and the implications for the emergence of IT solutions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
financialization in the public sector has been a driving force in the emergence of the e-ID solutions in all three countries.
the process model is a useful tool for understanding the dynamics and interplay between financialization and IT in the public sector, and the role of collective action theory as a theoretical lens.
the financial sector is an important stakeholder in the emergence of the national e-ID solutions, but not the only actor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
financialization in the public sector has the potential to create a win-win situation for all actors involved.
the process is driven forward by a combination of financialization, collective action, and institutional theory.
financialization is not a one-dimensional phenomenon but rather a complex process with multiple dimensions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
financialization is not necessarily a negative phenomenon, but can also be a source of positive change.
financialization can take three different paths, depending on the interests and resources of the involved actors.
different governance solutions for national e-ID solutions can be achieved, depending on how the actors interact and on the resources and interests that they possess.
